coverage_note: Louisiana has no comprehensive public-sector collective bargaining statute in the sources captured. La. R.S. 23:890 requires municipalities and transit authorities that acquire or operate public transportation facilities to bargain with and arbitrate disputes with their transit employees; other public employers may bargain voluntarily, which this row does not cover. The right-to-work Part, R.S. 23:981 to 987, applies to any person.

governing_statute.value: No comprehensive statute found. La. R.S. 23:890 covers employees of publicly acquired or operated public transportation facilities.
governing_statute.quote: B. Municipalities within the State of Louisiana hereafter acquiring, owning and/or operating public transportation facilities shall deal with and enter into written contracts with all employees of the said transportation facility, except executive and administrative employees, through accredited representatives of such employees or representatives of any labor organization authorized to act for such employees

source.publisher: Louisiana State Legislature, Louisiana Revised Statutes
source.title: RS 23:890

labor_board.null_reason: No Louisiana statute captured creates a public-sector labor relations board; R.S. 23:890 leaves recognition to the transit employer and disputes to ad hoc arbitration.

ulp_limitation_period.null_reason: No public-sector unfair labor practice procedure was found in Louisiana statutes captured for this row.

who_may_bargain.value: Employees of public transportation systems acquired or operated by a municipality, transit authority or similar authority, except executive and administrative employees. No statute captured gives other public employees a right to bargain.
who_may_bargain.quote: D. Employees of such public transportation systems hereafter acquired by any such municipality, transit authority or other authority organized for the purpose shall have the right to self organization, to form, join or assist labor organizations, to bargain collectively through representatives of their own choosing

scope_of_bargaining.value: For covered transit employees: wages, salaries, hours, working conditions and pension or retirement provisions.
scope_of_bargaining.quote: shall enter into a written contract with the accredited representative of such employees governing wages, salaries, hours and working conditions and pension and retirement provisions.

impasse_procedure.value: For covered transit employees: binding arbitration by a three-member board (one member chosen by each side, a neutral chair agreed on or picked from an American Arbitration Association list). No impasse procedure was found for other public employees.
impasse_procedure.quote: The determination of the majority of the board of arbitration thus established shall be final and binding on all matters in dispute.

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. Louisiana's right-to-work law bars requiring any person to pay union dues or fees as a condition of employment, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: No person shall be required, as a condition of employment, to become or remain a member of any labor organization, or to pay any dues, fees, assessments, or other charges of any kind to a labor organization.
